suggested_fix: Add at the end of Section 1.01 that any modification by Lessor to the Company's power and authority shall take effect prospectively only and shall not affect any Purchase Order already jointly acknowledged or Equipment already ordered or accepted under Section 2.01.

rationale: Section 1.01 appoints the Company solely as Lessor's unpaid agent to order Equipment 'on Lessor's behalf,' whereas Section 2.02 ('Receipt of and Payment for Equipment') obligates the Company 'to perform all obligations of the purchaser' under each Purchase Order, leaving unclear whether the Company must personally fund the purchase price without Lessor reimbursement or merely administer payment and delivery on Lessor's behalf.
suggested_fix: Clarify in Section 2.02 that the Company's obligation to perform purchaser obligations under a Purchase Order is carried out solely on Lessor's behalf and excludes any personal obligation to pay the purchase price except to the extent funded or reimbursed by Lessor.

rationale: Section 2(a) expressly permits Licensor to delete Licensed Programs during the Term upon 60 days' notice (subject to paying Rogers' reasonable costs or losses), which conflicts with Section 14(b)(ii)'s unqualified covenant that Licensor 'shall maintain throughout the Term, all necessary rights' for the Licensed Programs backed by Section 15(a)'s indemnity, while Section 14(b)(iv)'s 'unilaterally owns or controls' narrows Section 1's 'owns or controls'.
suggested_fix: Qualify Section 14(b)(ii) with 'Except for Licensed Programs duly deleted in accordance with Section 2(a),' and align Section 14(b)(iv) with Section 1 by replacing 'unilaterally owns or controls' with 'owns or controls' to the extent necessary to grant the non-exclusive license.

rationale: Clause 22(a)'s requirement to 'notify the other party as soon as practicable (and if possible prior to disclosure)' before compelled or third-party disclosure depends on Clause 26 ('NOTICES'), whose mandatory methods—personal delivery, registered mail, or facsimile immediately followed by registered mail—exclude electronic notice and could frustrate urgent pre-disclosure notification.
suggested_fix: Amend Clause 26 to permit urgent notices under Clause 22(a) (and Clause 25) to be given initially by email or telephone with immediate written confirmation by one of the formal delivery methods.

rationale: Clause 2's 3,000,000 monthly Impression guarantee defines 'Impression' by direct reference to the 'Tickets Portal' and 'above referenced pages' specified in Clause 1, and MP3.com's ability to deliver those Impressions depends on Tickets supplying compliant Portal content under Clause 1.
suggested_fix: Add to Clause 2 that MP3.com's guaranteed minimum Impression obligation is suspended to the extent and for the duration that Tickets fails to supply Portal content conforming to MP3.com's specifications under Clause 1.

rationale: Section 3 unconditionally obligates the Adviser to pay all specified Fund operating expenses, whereas Section 7 shields the Adviser from 'any damages, expenses or losses incurred by the Trust' arising out of 'payments made pursuant to this Agreement or any other matter to which this Agreement relates' absent willful misfeasance, bad faith, gross negligence, or reckless disregard, silently undermining strict contractual liability for non-payment or underpayment of expenses under Section 3.
suggested_fix: Add a proviso to Section 7 stating that nothing in Section 7 shall limit or excuse the Adviser's obligation to pay or reimburse Fund operating expenses assumed by the Adviser under Section 3.

rationale: Clause 11 excuses "any failure of performance hereunder" without carving out payment obligations or stating whether the fixed $5,000 monthly installments under Clause 6 ("In consideration of the services provided") abate if SRP's services are suspended by force majeure.
suggested_fix: Add to Clause 11 that force majeure does not excuse accrued payment obligations, provided that fixed monthly installments under Clause 6 shall abate pro rata during any period in which SRP is prevented from performing services due to force majeure.

rationale: Section 14.2 governs which obligations survive termination under Section 3.3 and explicitly enumerates Sections 3.5 and 4 (Charges) while omitting Sections 3.3 and 3.4(b), leaving IBM's waiver of early termination charges upon its own breach dependent on the general "without limitation" catch-all.
suggested_fix: Insert Sections 3.3 and 3.4(b) into the list of enumerated surviving provisions in Section 14.2 so that the bar on recovering early termination charges after an IBM breach expressly survives termination.

rationale: Section 1(b)'s automatic renewal depends on the $20 million "Net Sales (as defined below)" threshold and cross-references Section 7 for First Additional Term compensation, while Section 7(a)(i) defines "Net Sales" solely in terms of Licensed Products and ties royalty accrual to "the Term" defined in Section 1(a) as expiring July 22, 2016.
suggested_fix: Clarify in Section 1(a)-(b) that "Term" includes the First Additional Term and confirm in Section 7(a)(i) whether "Net Sales" for the First Renewal Threshold includes only Licensed Products.

rationale: Section 4(a)(ii) states that Endorser shall receive 10% of "Net Sales (as defined below)" of non-Licensed Products featured in the Training Video, whereas Section 7(a)(i) requires MusclePharm to pay Lender 10% on Net Sales of the Training Video and related Products while mis-citing Section 4(a)(i) and defining "Net Sales" exclusively in terms of Licensed Products.
suggested_fix: Align Sections 4(a)(ii) and 7(a)(i) to specify a single payee (Lender or Endorser), correct the cross-reference to Section 4(a)(ii), and expand the "Net Sales" definition in Section 7(a)(i) to cover the Training Video and non-Licensed Products sold in connection with it.

rationale: While Section 10 ties expense reimbursement to any "Appearance or Production Day" under Section 4(a), Section 11(a) restricts audit rights to records "with respect to the Licensed Products," leaving a gap regarding verification of the 10% royalty on non-Licensed Products sold in conjunction with the Training Video under Section 4(a)(ii).
suggested_fix: Amend Section 11(a) to extend the AS Parties' audit rights to books and records relating to the Training Video and any Products sold in conjunction with it under Section 4(a)(ii), as well as reimbursable expenses under Section 10.

rationale: Section 3.4 directly modifies Section 3.3 by reducing the tiered royalties upon an adverse Regulatory Authority determination, and Section 3.5 triggers sales milestone payments based on "Annual Net Sales, as detailed in Section 3.3," without specifying whether the Section 3.4 reduction is relative or percentage-point or whether Section 3.5 tracks annual or cumulative thresholds.
suggested_fix: Specify in Section 3.4 that the reduction applies proportionately to each royalty tier in Section 3.3 and clarify in Section 3.5 whether each milestone threshold is measured per calendar year under Section 3.3 or cumulatively.

rationale: Section 1.77 computes "Net Sales" solely on sales and resales by "Vyera or its Affiliates," leaving unclear both whether Affiliates are permitted to sell Licensed Products despite Section 2.1(a)-(b) granting rights only to Vyera without transfer or sublicensing, and whether sales by permitted sublicensees under Section 2.1(b) are included in Net Sales.
suggested_fix: Align Sections 1.77 and 2.1 by stating whether Vyera's Affiliates may exercise license rights without CytoDyn's separate consent under Section 2.1(b) and explicitly including sales by permitted sublicensees in the Section 1.77 definition of "Net Sales."

rationale: Clause A makes the Agreement "in all respects be subject to" Transporter's FERC Gas Tariff and deems it to include any unilateral Section 4 changes to "any rates, charges or provisions," creating uncertainty over whether such filings override a non-maximum rate agreed in writing under Clause B's Paragraph 9 or Appendix B.
suggested_fix: Add at the end of Section 12: "provided, however, that nothing in this Section 12 shall authorize Transporter to unilaterally alter any negotiated or discounted rate expressly agreed to by the parties in writing under Paragraph 9 or Appendix B hereto."

rationale: Section 5.1 of Clause B requires manufacture under lowercase-redefined "cGMPs" and undefined "the Specifications" rather than Clause A's defined terms "cGMP" (Section 1.6) and "Product Specifications" (Section 1.11), and Section 4.5 bars terms in "any other document" without expressly carving out the "Quality Agreement" defined in Section 1.12.
suggested_fix: Amend Section 5.1 to reference "cGMP, the Product Specifications, the Quality Agreement, and Applicable Laws" and add at the end of Section 4.5: "other than the Quality Agreement."

rationale: Section 4.4 of Clause A requires INTERSECT to pay within 30 calendar days of invoice upon dispatch with no withholding right, whereas Section 5.6 of Clause B gives INTERSECT 30 calendar days from arrival to inspect and reject non-conforming API and makes replacement HOVIONE's "sole responsibility" without addressing payment suspension or refund/credit for rejected lots.
suggested_fix: Add to Section 4.4 that INTERSECT may withhold payment for any lot timely rejected as non-conforming under Section 5.6 until HOVIONE delivers conforming replacement API or a neutral third-party testing laboratory determines that the lot materially conforms to the Product Specifications.

rationale: Section 5.6 of Clause B makes replacement within 30 days HOVIONE's "sole responsibility" for non-conforming API, leaving it unclear whether repeated non-conforming deliveries or failure to replace within 30 days constitute a material breach entitling INTERSECT to terminate under Section 10.2(a)(i) of Clause A and whether the 90-day cure period runs concurrently with or after the 30-day replacement window.
suggested_fix: Amend Section 5.6 to state that HOVIONE's replacement obligation is without prejudice to INTERSECT's termination rights under Section 10.2 if HOVIONE fails to replace non-conforming API within 30 days or repeatedly delivers non-conforming lots.

rationale: Section 2.4's right for Village Media Company to sublicense Exploitation of PFHOF Works and production of HOFV Works to "any of its Affiliates" operates through Section 1.2's closed list of 13 named HOFV entities (and Section 1.3's definition of "Exploit"), excluding any newly formed controlled subsidiaries of Village Media Company unlike PFHOF's open-ended Affiliate definition.
suggested_fix: Amend Section 1.2 to include after the enumerated entities "and any other entity directly or indirectly controlled by, or under common control with, HOFV from time to time."

rationale: Both Section 1 and Section 4 designate the Joint Venture's principal place of business at "1600 Lower State Road, Doylestown, PA," duplicating the address while differing on the ZIP code ("18901" in Section 1) versus "Bucks County" and the power to maintain other offices in Section 4.
suggested_fix: Delete the second sentence of Section 1 regarding the principal office and place of business so that Section 4 exclusively governs the Joint Venture's offices.

rationale: Section 4.3 explicitly governs claims brought "under paragraph 4.1 or 4.2," conditioning Section 4.1's indemnity for "any counsel fees" on notice and cutting off subsequent legal expenses if the indemnifying party assumes the defense, while leaving notice deadlines, consequences of late notice, and settlement-consent authority unspecified.
suggested_fix: Amend Section 4.3 to require prompt written notice of any claim (providing that delay relieves the indemnifying party only to the extent materially prejudiced) and to prohibit either party from settling any claim without the other's prior written consent unless the settlement unconditionally releases the indemnified party without admission of fault or non-monetary obligation.

rationale: Clause B requires Playboy's written signature for any binding "modification, termination or waiver", which depends on Clause A's designation of Playboy as a non-party "intended third-party beneficiary" and is vulnerable under Indian privity rules barring non-parties from restricting bilateral alteration or rescission by the contracting parties.
suggested_fix: Make Playboy a signatory party to this Contract in Clause A (or execute a direct tripartite undertaking) and revise Clause B so that Playboy's consent applies as an express contracting party.

rationale: Clause A's production and Playboy Properties restrictions are drafted strictly between Supplier and Purchaser, so Playboy's ability to directly enforce those covenants depends on Clause B's "intended third-party beneficiary" status, which lacks privity of contract under Indian law.
suggested_fix: State in Clause A that Supplier's covenants regarding Playboy Properties are also given directly to Playboy as a signatory party (or held by Purchaser in trust for Playboy) and align Clause B accordingly.

rationale: Clause A fixes a "one year engagement" governing Clause B's "duration of this agreement" monthly fees and product supply, yet Clause B(iii) leaves stock options in place "as long as the CELEBRITY maintains the distributorship by paying the annual dues of $15.00", making it unclear whether option vesting and "Monthly Sales Volume" targets survive the one-year term.
suggested_fix: Add to Clause B(iii) an explicit statement specifying whether stock option eligibility and Monthly Sales Volume calculations terminate at the end of the one-year engagement in Clause A or survive independently through the distributorship, and define how Monthly Sales Volume is measured.

rationale: Clause A makes the distributorship "independent of the endorsement terms of the agreement" and "on going" indefinitely, while Clause B requires mutual indemnification for "any action or a breach of any... agreement of the other party to this Agreement" alongside a "full release of liability" for product-use lawsuits, leaving unclear whether Clause B covers ongoing distributorship claims or bars Company indemnity claims arising from Celebrity's promotional statements.
suggested_fix: Clarify in Clause B whether the mutual indemnity survives for claims arising out of the ongoing distributorship under Clause A and specify that Celebrity's product-performance release does not excuse unauthorized product or income representations made while promoting the distributorship.

rationale: Clause B (4.4) conditions placement of the Wet Segment Supply Contract on "approval by the Management Committee", which depends on Clause A's establishment and meeting-notice rules for the Management Committee while Clause A omits the voting threshold required for non-emergency committee approvals.
suggested_fix: Specify in Clause A the voting threshold and deemed-approval or deadlock-resolution timeline governing Management Committee approvals required under Clause B (4.4).

rationale: Clause A preserves pre-termination obligations "arising under this Agreement" while Clause B "supersedes, cancels and terminates" Service Agreement FT18150 as of the effective date without a corresponding carve-out, leaving it ambiguous whether accrued payment or liability obligations under FT18150 survive supersession.
suggested_fix: Add to Clause B that termination and supersession of Service Agreement FT18150 is without prejudice to any rights, payment obligations, or liabilities accrued thereunder prior to the effective date of this Agreement.

rationale: Clause B excuses the Sponsor from liability for any 'error of judgment or mistake of law' or ordinary negligence in 'the performance of its duties hereunder,' directly narrowing the enforceability of the administrative and regulatory compliance oversight duties imposed in Clause A.
suggested_fix: Amend Section 4 to carve out breaches of statutory or regulatory filing obligations under Section 1(d) and require the Sponsor to exercise reasonable skill and diligence in performing its duties.

rationale: Clause B's Section 10 provides that Clause A's representations and warranties survive 'delivery of and payment for the Offered Shares,' while Section 9 terminates the Agreement without liability if not sold by May 26, 2016 'except as provided in Section 10,' leaving unclear which Clause A obligations survive an unconsummated termination under Section 9.
suggested_fix: Clarify in Section 10 whether the representations and warranties in Section 1 also survive a termination without sale under Section 9 or only survive delivery of and payment for the Offered Shares.

rationale: Clause A requires formal milestone-based status updates for the deliverables in Sections 6.1-6.4, which depend on Clause B's Section 6.5 milestone table ('as per the points mentioned above'), yet Section 6.5 omits the timeline for the final completion milestone and leaves 'VAL's business compliance' undefined.
suggested_fix: Specify a concrete completion deadline for the fourth milestone row in Section 6.5 and define the scope of 'VAL's business compliance' relative to the graphics and content supplied by VAL under Clause A.

rationale: Clause A's Section 2.2(a) allows Todos to cancel the Reseller's exclusivity upon missing 50% of an Annual Milestone while leaving the Reseller non-exclusive, whereas Clause B's Section 4.12 prohibits the Reseller from selling competing products or serving any direct competitor without clarifying whether that restraint ends once exclusivity is revoked.
suggested_fix: Add a proviso to Section 4.12 stating that the non-compete restriction ceases to apply if Todos cancels the Reseller's exclusivity under Section 2.2(a), and confine the restriction strictly to competing Products during exclusivity.

rationale: Clause A's Section 15 permits assignment of rights under the Agreement with prior written approval 'which shall not be unreasonably withheld,' whereas Clause B's Section 3 bars recognizing any assignee or transferee of the Bonus Warrant or underlying shares absent an effective registration statement or an opinion of counsel 'satisfactory to the Company' without a reasonableness standard.
suggested_fix: Clarify in Section 15 that transfers of the Warrants and underlying shares are governed by Section 3, and state in Section 3 that acceptance of a compliant securities-law opinion of counsel shall not be unreasonably withheld.

rationale: Clause A calculates Fox's royalty on Licensee's 'Gross Receipts' for 'IA2 Audio and Video Wireless Products,' while Clause B governs direct VGSL/CSP payments to Fox for 'IA Audio and Video Wireless Products' without clarifying whether 'IA' means 'IA2' or whether those direct remittances are excluded from or credited against Licensee's Gross Receipts.
suggested_fix: Correct 'IA Audio and Video Wireless Products' in Section 2 to 'IA2 Audio and Video Wireless Products' and state expressly whether direct VGSL/CSP payments to Fox are excluded from Gross Receipts under Section 1(a) or credited against the IA2 Audio and Video Royalty.

rationale: Section 8 excludes 'any Defaulting Sponsor' from pro rata distribution of a Termination Fee, which depends directly on Section 3's definition of 'Defaulting Sponsor' and determination of failure to comply with the Equity Commitment Letter and this Agreement.
suggested_fix: Clarify in Section 8 that a Sponsor is excluded from Termination Fee distributions only if its participation has been validly terminated under Section 3 following notice and an opportunity to cure its funding default.

rationale: Section 4.4's exhaustive survival list ('Sections 1.4, 3, 4.4, 5.1, 5.2, and 6.1 through 6.11') omits Section 1.2's goodwill and no-ownership acknowledgment as well as Section 1.1's Transition Period use restrictions, leaving post-termination ownership acknowledgments and wind-down rights unclear.
suggested_fix: Amend Section 4.4 to include Section 1.2 and any applicable post-termination Transition Period terms of Section 1.1 among the provisions that survive expiration or termination of this Agreement.

rationale: Section 4.4 expressly provides that Section 3 (Indemnification) survives expiration or termination while omitting Section 1.6 (trademark usage guidelines) and Section 2 (third-party infringement notice and assistance), terminating Licensor's enforcement assistance rights even for pre-termination claims.
suggested_fix: Amend Section 4.4 to add that Section 2 shall also survive expiration or termination solely with respect to infringement or claims arising out of acts occurring prior to the effective date of expiration or termination.

rationale: Section 1.5's Right of Recovery operates entirely through Section 1.1's definition of 'Expense Waiver' and zero-floor Net Investment Income threshold, permitting indefinite recovery (and parallel Underwriter reimbursement) whenever Net Investment Income exceeds zero without a lookback limit or priority rule.
suggested_fix: Amend Section 1.5 to cap Expense Waiver recovery to amounts waived or reimbursed within the preceding three years and specify the pro rata or priority allocation between the Investment Adviser and the Underwriter.

rationale: Section 2 ties fees to the Services and Exhibit A pricing in Section 1, but upon termination other than under Section 3 obligates Diplomat to pay full Exhibit A fees for the balance of the Period 'as though Tadeo continued to provide the terminated Services,' operating as an unenforceable penalty without proof of actual loss under Indian law.
suggested_fix: Replace the post-termination acceleration wording in Section 2 with a genuine pre-estimate of damages or actual substantiated losses suffered by Tadeo, subject to a duty to mitigate and excluding unearned service costs.

rationale: The Farids Group's Demand Registration right under Section 6.1 (exercisable on or after the second anniversary) is conditioned on furnishing information within one business day under Section 6.10 and terminates entirely under Section 6.11 once its ownership falls below 3% after the Expiration Date.
suggested_fix: Clarify in Section 6.11 that any Demand Request validly submitted under Section 6.1 prior to the Farids Group's ownership falling below 3% shall remain effective until the related registration is completed.

rationale: Although Section 6.1 obligates the Company to register 'all Registrable Securities' requested by the Farids Group, Section 6.3 ('Notwithstanding any other provision of this Article VI') subjects Section 6.1 registrations to underwriter marketing cutbacks and priority allocation rules.
suggested_fix: Amend Section 6.1(a) to add 'and Section 6.3' after 'subject to the provisions of Section 6.1(c)' and clarify whether a cutback registration still counts as one of the two Demand Requests.

rationale: Section 1(a) obligates the Sponsor to maintain office facilities and furnish clerical services, whereas Section 2 requires the Trust to pay 'all of its operating expenses' except salaries of Domini-affiliated personnel, leaving unclear whether office space and clerical overhead under Section 1(a) are included in the Sponsor's fee or chargeable to the Trust.
suggested_fix: Add to Section 2 that Domini shall bear all costs of the office facilities and clerical services furnished under Section 1(a) and that such overhead shall not be charged as operating expenses of the Trust.

rationale: Section 11.1 in Clause A mandates binding arbitration for any dispute involving the construction or application of the Agreement (except Section 11.2) and splits arbitrator costs, whereas Section 12.8 in Clause B awards prevailing-party attorneys' fees in "any court action at law or equity... to enforce or interpret the provisions of this Agreement," leaving unclear whether court actions at law are permitted or whether fee-shifting applies in arbitration.
suggested_fix: Amend Section 12.8 in Clause B to clarify that the prevailing party is entitled to reasonable attorneys' fees and costs in any arbitration under Section 11.1 or any permitted court proceeding under Section 11.2 or to enforce an arbitral award.

rationale: Both Clause A and Clause B purport to amend the exact same "Section 2" Territory definition ("is amended to be the United States and [*]" vs "is amended to be United States, [*]") without cross-referencing each other, inviting inconsistency over whether Clause B replaces or supplements Clause A's territory scope.
suggested_fix: Amend Clause B to expressly reference and supersede the prior amendment to Section 2 and restate the complete consolidated list of covered territories.

rationale: Clause A (Amendment #2) states that "all other provisions of the Agreement remain unchanged" while the Amendment #2 preamble in Clause B defines "Agreement" solely as the October 1, 1996 original Distribution Agreement, leaving ambiguous whether Amendment #1's changes referenced in Clause B remain in force or are excluded.
suggested_fix: Revise Amendment #2 in Clause A and its preamble to define "Agreement" as the Distribution Agreement dated October 1, 1996, as amended by Amendment #1, and confirm that Amendment #1 remains in effect except as modified by Amendment #2.

rationale: Section 5 in Clause A ties Surgical's IP disclosure and ownership obligations to inventions developed from "Confidential Information (as defined in the Confidentiality Agreement," which depends on the parties concurrently executing the separate Exhibit A Confidentiality Agreement mandated by Section 6 in Clause B, while Section 5.4 in Clause B governs post-termination delivery of the Work Product covered by Section 5.
suggested_fix: Expressly cross-reference Section 6 and Exhibit A in Section 5 and clarify that execution of the Confidentiality Agreement is a condition concurrent to disclosure and IP vesting, or incorporate the definition of Confidential Information directly into the Agreement.

rationale: Section 15 in Clause A enumerates "Sections 2, 5, 6, 9-20" as surviving termination while omitting Sections 3 and 4 (Sales Commissions and 60-day post-quarter reporting and remittance "during the Term"), leaving ambiguous whether Surgical's right to earned or final-quarter Sales Commissions survives termination under Section 15's general catch-all.
suggested_fix: Amend Section 15 in Clause A to expressly include Sections 3 and 4 (with respect to Sales Commissions accrued or attributable to Product sales prior to termination) in the list of surviving provisions.

rationale: Section 15 in Clause A governs which provisions in Clause B survive termination, expressly continuing Section 5 (including Section 5.4's obligation to deliver all Work Product "promptly upon termination") and Section 6 (Confidentiality), while omitting Section 7 (Conflicts of Interest) from the enumerated surviving sections.
suggested_fix: Add Section 7 to Section 15 only if the parties intend Section 7 representations and warranties to survive termination; otherwise no change is required.

rationale: Clause 3.6 unconditionally bars the Manufacturer from selling any Schedule A product or product name to another party without the Customer's prior written consent, overlapping with differing terms in Clauses 13.1 and 13.2 that condition the Customer's exclusive rights (including indefinite continuation beyond 10 years) on fulfilling Schedule B minimum annual purchase requirements, while Clause 3.5(b) also designates named Medical Team individuals as Manufacturer Intellectual Property without clarifying how Clause 12's IP right of first refusal applies to them.
suggested_fix: Amend Clause 3.6 to state that the Manufacturer's non-sale covenant applies only during the subsistence of the Customer's exclusive rights under Clauses 13.1 and 13.2 and remains subject to the Customer fulfilling Schedule B minimum annual purchase requirements, and clarify in Clause 3.5(b) that individual consultants are excluded from transferable IP under Clause 12.

rationale: Clause 5.3 requires the Customer to notify the Manufacturer of defective-product rejections within seven days of receipt or be deemed to have accepted the Products, which depends on Clause 14.1's Notice rules that exclude e-mail and deem ordinary mail served one day after posting, effectively compressing the rejection window.
suggested_fix: Add to Clause 5.3 that rejection notices and RMA requests may be delivered by e-mail in addition to the methods in Clause 14.1 and shall be deemed given when sent within the seven-day period.

rationale: Clause 13.1 appoints the Customer as the "sole and exclusive agent", whereas Clause 6.1 places the product liability insurance and Customer indemnity obligations on "The Manufacturing Companies utilised by the Agent to manufacture the products", creating ambiguity as to who bears product liability and indemnity responsibility (while Clause 7.2's 21-day cure period from breach notification also depends on Clause 14.1's deemed-service rules).
suggested_fix: Replace "The Manufacturing Companies utilised by the Agent" and "the company" in Clause 6.1 with "The Manufacturer" so that the Manufacturer directly maintains product liability insurance and indemnifies the Customer.

rationale: Clauses 7.1–7.2 (restricting solicitation of employees and prohibiting providing competitive products or services to Customers for 12 months post-termination) and Clause 7.3 (barring any involvement with or services for a Competitor for 12 months post-termination) overlap with differing scopes to impose post-termination restraints on trade that are void under Indian law.
suggested_fix: Limit the competitive restrictions in Clauses 7.2(a) and 7.3 to the duration of the consultancy only, and confine post-termination covenants to non-solicitation of employees and non-disclosure of Proprietary Information.

rationale: Clause 4.1 identifies SIC as an entity "to be formed" structured around "tribal sovereignty", which leaves an unresolved jurisdictional and capacity gap when read with Clause 11.5's submission to Florida law, non-binding arbitration ("If arbitration fails to render a mutually agreement resolution"), and the Courts of the State of Florida without any waiver of sovereign immunity or corporate ratification mechanism.
suggested_fix: Amend Clauses 4.1 and 11.5 to require formal execution and ratification by SIC upon incorporation, include an express limited waiver of tribal sovereign immunity for dispute resolution and enforcement, and stipulate that the arbitral award shall be final and binding.

rationale: Clause 5.4 states that the decision to join the alliance is at SIC management's absolute discretion without any claim by TKCI if SIC decides not to sign in the investigation stage, leaving it uncertain how Clause 9.3's restriction on early termination only by mutual written agreement or for cause and its one-year post-termination confidentiality survival apply if SIC unilaterally declines to proceed.
suggested_fix: Clarify in Clauses 5.4 and 9.3 that SIC's investigation-stage discretion applies to executing subsequent project agreements or constitutes an express ground for termination of this Agreement without liability, while preserving TKCI's confidentiality obligations under Clause 9.3 upon such withdrawal.

rationale: Section 6 assigns all inventions, compounds, and data developed "in performance of the Services" or "in connection with work under this Agreement," but Section 1 describes Services only as open-ended advice on research, clinical development, and "other business matters as requested by Aduro from time to time," leaving the boundary between assigned Work Product and Consultant's independent research uncertain.

suggested_fix: Replace the survival sentence in Section 10 with an explicit enumeration of the sections (such as intellectual property, confidentiality, and accrued payment obligations) that survive expiration or termination of this Agreement under Section 3.

rationale: Section 14(b) and 14(c) warrant completion and substantial conformance of the Ehave Companion Solution for the duration of the Term, whereas Section 3(a) acknowledges that the Specifications and Implementation Plan may not yet be developed at execution and must be approved later in writing, leaving the benchmark for the warranty uncertain if the Parties fail to agree.

rationale: Clause A defers due diligence confirmation and signing of the Technical Appendix (which sets the design and evaluation standards referenced in Clause B's 20-year term and monthly fee trigger) to 90 days post-signing while Clause A(4) forbids termination except by mutual written agreement, leaving unclear whether the 20-year obligations or fees fall away or can be exited upon non-satisfaction or payment default.

suggested_fix: Add language in paragraph 4 requiring AIG to use reasonable best efforts to obtain all necessary board and regulatory approvals in advance of the paragraph 3 funding windows and clarifying AIG's alternative funding obligations if an approval is delayed.

rationale: Clause B expressly conditions policyholder enforcement of AIG's contribution duties under Clause A ("paragraphs 1, 3 and 4") on a 60-day notice-and-cure period and limits post-termination survival to pre-termination obligations under those paragraphs, leaving unclear whether the 60-day cure period extends Clause A's fixed quarterly funding windows.
suggested_fix: Clarify in paragraph 8 that the sixty-day policyholder notice period is without prejudice to AIG's obligation to fund within the timeframes specified in paragraph 3 and does not extend those deadlines.

rationale: Clause A (Clause 18) provides that the late-delivery penalty "shall be deducted by the paying bank from the payment," whereas Clause B (Clause 11) mandates payment either by a 100% irrevocable letter of credit payable against specified Clause 12 documents (which omit any penalty deduction mechanism) or by telegraphic transfer where no paying bank administers L/C deductions.
suggested_fix: Amend Clause 18 and Clause 11/12 to provide that any late-delivery liquidated damages (pre-estimated loss) shall either be deducted directly by the Sellers on the commercial invoice or paid/credited separately by the Sellers upon Buyer's demand rather than withheld unilaterally by an L/C paying bank.

rationale: Clause A defines "Confidential Information" to include "all Inventions (as defined below)" from Clause B, while Clause B defines "Inventions" to encompass items conceived or reduced to practice "through the use of Confidential Information," creating a mutual cross-definition where Clause A's prior-knowledge exceptions must not undermine Clause B's IP ownership.
suggested_fix: Clarify in Section 2 that the exceptions to confidentiality do not limit Company's ownership of Inventions under Section 3, and expressly exclude Consultant's pre-existing independent intellectual property from both definitions.

rationale: Clause B's termination and full-refund trigger ("If the proposed price Is Increased by Supplier upon delivery to Bank of America of detailed specifications") depends directly on the specification delivery and Bank of America approval process in Clause A, leaving unaddressed whether price increases resulting from Bank of America's own specification changes also trigger a 100% refund.
suggested_fix: Clarify in Section 4 and Section 1 whether Bank of America's termination and full-refund right applies only to unilateral Supplier price increases unrelated to Bank of America-requested scope changes, and specify a deadline for exercising termination after delivery of the detailed specifications.

rationale: Section 5.9 limits CBC's free storage of Bromelain SP batches at its premises to 90 days from the Acceptance Sample Notice, while Section 6.2 requires CBC at all times to maintain an inventory of Bromelain SP at its premises equal to a percentage of the Annual Forecast, leaving unclear whether Section 6.2 buffer inventory is subject to Section 5.9's 90-day free-storage cap or triggers storage charges.
suggested_fix: Clarify in Sections 5.9 and 6.2 that the 90-day free-storage period in Section 5.9 applies only to Bromelain SP batches allocated to accepted purchase orders and does not entitle CBC to charge storage fees for buffer inventory maintained under Section 6.2.

rationale: Section 11.1 and Section 11.2 only preserve rights and obligations accrued as of termination and remedies for breach without cross-referencing Section 8, while Section 8.3 establishes independent post-termination confidentiality and non-use obligations for five years after termination (and in perpetuity for Product and IP Confidential Information) triggered by termination under Section 10.2 or 10.3.
suggested_fix: Amend Section 11.1 to expressly state that, in addition to accrued rights and obligations, the confidentiality and non-use obligations under Section 8.3 shall survive termination or expiry of the Agreement in accordance with their terms.

rationale: Both Section 2.1 and Sections 11.1–11.2 govern ALFA AESAR's reasonable-efforts and exclusivity obligations during the term, but Section 2.1 conditions exclusive purchasing on NTC supplying Products and covers substantially similar nanomaterials without exception, whereas Section 11.2 imposes an unconditional restriction on products with the same specifications while carving out preexisting ALFA AESAR products.
suggested_fix: Harmonize Sections 2.1 and 11.2 so both apply the same product-scope definition, preserve the carve-out for preexisting ALFA AESAR products, and suspend exclusivity if NTC fails to supply Products, while consolidating the duplicate reasonable-efforts requirement.

rationale: Section 6.3's post-termination right for ALFA AESAR to audit NTC's referral records within 12 months operates through Section 13.2's survival clause stating that Section 6 survives termination, though Section 6.3 restricts the audit trigger to when the agreement "has been terminated by the parties" whereas Sections 13.2–13.3 address termination "for any reason."
suggested_fix: Amend Section 6.3 to replace "has been terminated by the parties" with "expires or is terminated for any reason" and clarify that Section 6 survives only for the twelve-month post-termination audit and settlement period.

rationale: Clause 1 sets a three-season term from the first race of the 1998 Winston Cup season through the final race of the 2000 season, whereas Clause 2 obligates Sabco to perform services "during the term hereof" but specifies drivers, car numbers, and sponsorship display only for "the 33 Winston Cup events to be held during the 1998 season," leaving the 1999 and 2000 seasons undefined.
suggested_fix: Amend Sections 2.A and 2.B to specify the covered Winston Cup events, car numbers, and driver lineup (or selection mechanism) applicable to the 1999 and 2000 seasons in addition to the 1998 season.

rationale: Section 2 grants the Employee the exclusive right (exercisable by sole signature) over excess proceeds and beneficiary designations, yet Section 4 makes "[a]ny payment directed by the Owner under this endorsement" a full discharge of the Insurer binding on all parties claiming under the policy without limiting that discharge to the Owner's Section 1 interest.
suggested_fix: Amend Section 4 so that the Insurer's full discharge applies solely to payments directed by the Owner in respect of the Owner's interest under Section 1, and does not prejudice or bind Section 2 beneficiaries as to excess proceeds without the Employee's written consent.

rationale: Section 1.3 defines "Equivalent Quantity" to be delivered to Shipper as received gas "less Fuel Usage and Applicable Shrinkage," making Shipper's deliverable quantity directly dependent on Section 1.4, which lets Transporter retain uncapped gas for leakage, blow-down, and lost and unaccounted-for gas.
suggested_fix: Amend Section 1.4 to cap Fuel Usage and Applicable Shrinkage at the percentage specified in Transporter's FERC Gas Tariff and exclude losses caused by Transporter's negligence or willful misconduct.

rationale: Section 6.1 depends on Section 2.2 to identify which rate schedule applies, but Section 2.2 marks "X" for Rate Schedule FTS without deleting "firm/interruptible" and Section 6.1 leaves "FTS/ITS Rate Schedule" unedited, creating uncertainty over the applicable service and fee schedule.
suggested_fix: Strike "/interruptible" in Section 2.2 and "/ITS" in Section 6.1 so both clauses unambiguously specify firm service under Transporter's Rate Schedule FTS.

rationale: Clause 1(c) requires Integrity to obtain master lease and print agreements "at its own expense," whereas Clause 3(a) includes "Master Lease royalty" and "Copyright royalty" in the unit pricing charged to TL and allows Integrity to adjust TL's prices to reflect "the then-current royalty obligation," leaving unclear which party ultimately bears those royalty costs.
suggested_fix: Clarify in Clause 1(c) that Integrity's obligation to obtain third-party master lease and print agreements "at its own expense" covers upfront clearance and administrative costs only, without limiting the per-unit royalty components and price adjustments payable by TL under Clause 3(a).

rationale: Clause 10.3 expires the IP licence "at the end of the Term" while Clause 15.3.2 requires ceasing IP use and returning or destroying IP materials only "On termination" (omitting expiry, unlike Clause 15.4), and Clause 15.4.1 leaves survival of Clauses 10.1, 10.4, and 11 to an unenumerated "by its very nature should survive" standard.
suggested_fix: Amend Clause 10.3 and Clause 15.3.2 to state that the licence terminates and branded materials must be returned or destroyed upon either termination or expiry of the Agreement, and expressly enumerate Clauses 10.1, 10.4, and 11 in Clause 15.4.1 as surviving provisions.

rationale: Clause 3(b) allows resales in conformity with "Rule 145(d)" or "some other exemption," whereas Clause 4's restrictive legend narrows Rule 145(d) to non-affiliates of PSS (requiring "Rule 144" for PSS affiliates) and conditions other exemptions on "a legal opinion satisfactory to counsel for PSS."
suggested_fix: Conform Clause 3(b)(2)-(3) to Clause 4 by specifying that Rule 145(d) applies only while the undersigned is not a PSS affiliate (otherwise Rule 144 applies) and that reliance on any other exemption requires a legal opinion satisfactory to counsel for PSS.

rationale: Clause 4 imposes stop-transfer instructions and a legend barring transfers unless compliant with Rule 145(d), Rule 144, or an exemption backed by a legal opinion, while Clause 7 provides the transfer-agent representation and PSS-counsel opinion procedure only for sales under "Rule 145(d)," leaving transfers under Rule 144 or Clause 4(3) without an opinion-clearance obligation.
suggested_fix: Expand Clause 7 to require PSS to cause its counsel to issue transfer-agent clearance opinions on the same terms whenever the undersigned submits a compliant representation letter or satisfactory legal opinion for a transfer under Rule 144 or another applicable exemption permitted by Clause 4.

rationale: Clause 11 requires the Trust to pay "the aggregate amount of the premiums paid under the Policy since inception" to terminate and re-acquire the Policy without deducting proceeds already received by the Company from a surrender, withdrawal, or loan under Clause 3, and Clause 3 does not specify whether a complete surrender discharging those premiums terminates the Agreement or repays the Demand Note.
suggested_fix: Amend Clause 11 to credit any proceeds previously paid to the Company under Clause 3 against the Trust's termination payment, and clarify in Clause 3 whether a complete surrender or cancellation paying the Company its aggregate premiums terminates the Agreement and satisfies the Demand Note.

rationale: Paragraph 1 relies on Paragraph 3 for both AIG's contribution deadlines and the post-quarter estimation cutoff ("before such time as AIG would be obligated pursuant to paragraph 3"), while Paragraph 3's proviso allows pre-filing contributions for any quarter or year to be recognized retroactively on the yet-to-be-filed statutory statement without specifying how they affect Paragraph 1's filed-statement trigger and cutoff calculation.
suggested_fix: Clarify in Paragraph 3 that any pre-filing capital contribution recognized as a receivable on a quarterly or annual statutory financial statement under the proviso shall be included in Total Adjusted Capital for Paragraph 1's threshold test and credited against AIG's required contribution for the corresponding period.

rationale: Section 5(c) requires return or destruction of Confidential Information upon termination, yet Section 7(a) enumerates only Sections 3(g), 3(h), and 6 as surviving termination, leaving a gap as to whether Section 5(c) survives while Section 5(a)/(b) notice periods also depend on Section 7(d)'s deemed-delivery rules.
suggested_fix: Amend Section 7(a) to include "5(c)," in the list of provisions that survive termination indefinitely.

rationale: Clause 5.3 grants a 10-to-30-day cure period after an "Event of Default" occurs, whereas Clause 6.1 defines an Event of Default as arising only after expiration of notice and cure rights (including 3 Business Days for payment defaults in 6.1.1), creating a circular trigger and conflicting cure periods before termination.
suggested_fix: Amend Clause 5.3 to apply to a "breach or default" rather than an "Event of Default" and clarify in Clauses 5.3 and 6.1 that Clause 5.3 provides the sole cure period for Clause 6.1.2 without extending Clause 6.1.1's three-Business-Day payment cure window.

rationale: Section 2.5(iv) states that neither party shall be obligated for any debt, obligation, or liability of the other "Except as otherwise provided by the applicable law," omitting a carve-out for the Agreement itself and thereby contradicting Company's obligation under Section 9.5 to defend claims against Distributor.
suggested_fix: Amend the opening of Section 2.5(iv) to read "Except as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement (including Section 9) or by applicable law,".

rationale: Section 1 incorporates and requires compliance with "the Agreement" (including Section 2(ii)), whereas Section 3 declares that the terms "herein contained" constitute the entire agreement and "supersede any previous and contemporaneous agreements" without preserving the underlying Agreement.
suggested_fix: Insert "Except for the Agreement (as modified hereby)," at the beginning of Section 3 so the underlying Agreement referenced in Section 1 is not superseded.

rationale: Section 2 expressly keeps "the Agreement" in full force and effect subject to the modifications herein, while Section 3 states that the terms "herein contained" constitute the entire agreement and "supersede any previous and contemporaneous agreements" without carving out the Agreement.
suggested_fix: Amend Section 3 to begin with "Except for the Agreement, which remains in full force and effect as modified hereby, the terms and conditions herein contained...".

rationale: Paragraph 3 distinguishes natural expiry on December 31, 2020 from the Agreement being "earlier terminated," whereas Paragraph 7 runs the 12-month post-term Restricted Period only "after the termination of this Agreement," leaving unclear whether expiry on December 31, 2020 triggers it.
suggested_fix: Replace "after the termination of this Agreement" in Paragraph 7 with "after the expiration or earlier termination of this Agreement".

rationale: Both Section 1.4 and Sections 12.3–12.4 govern Distributor's trademark license, but they define "Trademarks" differently and Section 1.4 imposes an absolute bar on combining marks or sublicensing whereas Section 12.4 permits such uses and delegations with Company's prior written consent.
suggested_fix: Consolidate Sections 1.4 and 12.3–12.4 into a single trademark license clause with one uniform definition of "Trademarks" and align Section 1.4's absolute prohibitions on trade-name combination and delegation with Section 12.4's prior written consent exceptions.

rationale: Section 2.4.1(d) requires "any disputes" to be reviewed by Agreement Administrators and escalated to Designated Executives, while Section 8.5 entitles iBio to seek equitable relief from "any court" upon breach or threatened breach without clarifying whether internal escalation is a precondition to court action.
suggested_fix: Amend Section 8.5 to clarify that, notwithstanding the dispute review and escalation procedure in Section 2.4.1(d), iBio may apply directly to any court of competent jurisdiction for immediate injunctive or equitable relief.

rationale: Section 1(b) triggers automatic renewal based on $20 million Net Sales in the Third Contract Year and Section 11(b) mandates three-year post-termination/expiration record retention, yet Section 11(a) restricts audit rights to "once each Contract Year of the Term", leaving post-expiration verification of final-year sales unclear.
suggested_fix: Amend Section 11(a) to specify that the AS Parties' annual audit right survives expiration or termination of the Term for three years to match MusclePharm's record-retention period under Section 11(b) and allow verification of Third Contract Year Net Sales.

rationale: Section 2 expressly authorizes the use and disclosure of Confidential Information necessary to perform the Services, whereas Section 6 imposes mutual, uncapped, no-fault indemnification for any losses that "arise out of the services rendered by Business Affiliate", undercutting authorized performance under Section 2 and making UDC potentially liable for Business Affiliate's own services.
suggested_fix: Amend Section 6 so that Business Affiliate solely indemnifies UDC for losses arising from Business Affiliate's breach of this Agreement, unauthorized use or disclosure of Confidential Information, or negligent or wrongful performance of the Services, excluding compliant performance authorized under Section 2.

rationale: Section 3(d) incorporates a subcontractor return-or-destruction obligation "as provided under paragraph g of this Section 3", while Section 5(c) separately requires each Party and its subcontractors or agents to return or destroy all Confidential Information upon termination without cross-referencing Section 3(g), risking divergent terms and exceptions.
suggested_fix: Harmonize Sections 3(d)/3(g) and 5(c) by cross-referencing Section 5(c) in Section 3(d) (or consolidating all return-or-destruction rules, timelines, and legal-retention exceptions into Section 5(c)) so subcontractors and Parties are governed by one consistent post-termination obligation.
